full_judgment:
This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite-parties No. 1-4 to show cause as to why the judgment and order dated 6-3-1997 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge now Joint District Judge, First Court, Faridpur in Review Miscellaneous Case No. 33 of 1996 affirming the judgment and decree dated 6-4-1996 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge now Joint District Judge, First Court, Faridpur in Title Appeal No. 248 of 1983 affirming the judgment and decree dated 24-8-1983 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Sadar, Faridpur in Title Suit No. 183 of 1980 dismissing the suit should not be set aside. 

 3. The short facts of the plaintiffs case are that he purchased the suit land from Phoenix Chemical Laboratories through its Managing Director, Mr Mohiuddin Ahamed on 10-1-1971 by a registered saf kabala. Thereafter, on 12-3-1980 a modified sale deecl was executed by said Mr Mohiuddin Ahmed in favour of the appellant-petitioner who thus got right title in respect of 4.98 acres of land, the suit land. The defendant Government alleged that the suit land was the excess land of ex-landlord Kiran Chandra Lahiri who surrendered the same to the Government and the latter gave settlement of the said land to the defendant Nos. 2 and 3 and hence the plaintiff instituted the suit praying for declaration of his title to the suit land. 

 6. The plaintiff-appellant as petitioner being aggrieved by judgment and decree passed by the appellate Court below filed Review Miscellaneous Case No. 33 of 1996 in the Court of learned Joint District Judge, First Court, Faridpur under Order XLVII, rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure for review of the judgment and decree dated 6-4-1996 contending that Kiran Chandra Lahiri was not the Managing Director of Phoenix Chemical Laboratories on 30-3-1973 and at that time Zamini Kanto Lahiri was the Managing Director and thereafter, Mr Mohiuddin Ahmed was the Managing Director. Signature on the document of surrender purported to be the signature of Kiran Chandra Lahiri was forged. But even after exercise of due diligence the said fact could not be pressed at the time of hearing. 

 7. The opposite parties did not raise any objection in the said Miscellaneous Review case. 

 9. The Subordinate Judge now Joint District Judge, First Court, Faridpur hearing the petitioner by judgment and order dated 6-3-1997 disallowed the said case. Being dissatisfied with the same the petitioner preferred this revision application and obtained the instant Rule. 

 10. No one appeared for either of the par-ties. Nevertheless, the High Court Division can exercise its revisional jurisdiction under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure either at the instance of party or suo moto. I may quote here profitably the decision in the case of Safaruddin vs Fazlid Haque reported in 49 DLR (AD) 151 where the Appellate Division held as follows: 

 11. Thus even in the absence of any of the parties High Court Division under its supervisory power as contemplated in section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure can dispose of the matter on consideration of the facts and circumstance of the case. Accordingly, I have taken up this Rule for hearing and disposal though none appeared for either of the parties. 

 12. The petitioner filed the Miscellaneous Review case under Order XLVII, rule 1 of the Code of Civil. Procedure for review of the judgment and order dated 6-4-1996 passed in Title Appeal No. 248 of 1983 contending that the sale deeds Exhibit 6 and 6 ka was executed by Mr Mohiuddin Ahmed, the Managing Director of Phoenix Chemical Laboratories. The surrender document was purportedly executed under the signature of Kiron Chandra Lahiri styling himself as Managing Director of the said Laboratories was false and forged and the same being new important matter which even after exercise of due diligence was not within his knowledge. 

 15. In this context I may refer the case of Noor Hossain vs Bangladesh reported in 49 DLR (AD) 108 where the Appellate Division has said in the following terms: 

 16. The Appellate Division in the case of Abul Hossain vs Bangladesh reported in 51 DLR (AD) 116 has decided as under: 

 17. I have perused the revision application and the judgment and order under challenge. From the materials on record, it appears that the suit land admittedly auction purchased by the defendant No.6, the Phoenix Chemical Laboratories in Certificate Case No 4056 A-BK/ 60-61 on getting sale certificate and writ of delivery of possession. The petitioner contended that Kiran Chandra Lahiri was not the Managing Director on the date of alleged execution of the document of surrender and his purported signature therein was forged. 

 18. Respective parties in the suit adduced both oral and documentary evidence which were marked exhibits. The petitioner was required to prove his case by evidence that Kiran Chandra Laheri was not the Managing Director of the Company on the date of surrender. But he failed to discharge his legal obligation to prove that be could not produce the said evidence before the Courts below after exercise of reasonable care and due diligence which was not within his knowledge. Reading the grounds for review taken in the petition of Review Miscellaneous Case No.33 of 1996 it appears that the petitioner sought opportunity for rehearing of the matter sitting over its own judgment passed by the appellate Court which is not permissible in law as provided in Order XLVII, rule I of the Code as well as the decisions referred to hereinabove. 

 20. In view of the discussions made above I do not find that the Joint District Judge committed any error of law resulting in an error occasioning failure of justice in passing the impugned order dated 6-3-1997 disallowing the Review Miscellaneous Case No. 33 of 1996 and hence does not warrant any interference by this Court in revision.
